title: Supervised Rare-event Modeling
interviewAnswer: When rare-event labels exist, treat the problem as cost-sensitive classification with careful temporal splits, sampling/weighting and precision-recall evaluation rather than unsupervised anomaly detection.
keyPoints: Calibrate/adjust probabilities if training distribution changes.
Use event-time split to avoid leakage.
why: Supervised Rare-event Modeling is a recurring foundation across data science and machine learning because it affects both theoretical correctness and practical system behavior.

The interview-level skill is not merely recalling the definition: explain the assumptions, what diagnostic evidence you would inspect, and what alternative you would choose when those assumptions fail.
workedExample: Train a failure classifier on 1% positives using weighted loss and evaluate recall at a fixed false-alert budget.
commonMistakes: Using the concept mechanically without checking assumptions or data semantics.
